# AI Report Template with Guardrails

**Purpose:** Template for any AI-generated analysis, benchmark results, recommendations, or documentation in the Librio project.

**Key principle:** All AI-generated content must be clearly marked, evidence-based, and include explicit confidence levels and limitations.

---

## Report Header (Required)

```markdown
# [Report Title]

**Generated by:** [AI model / tool]  
**Date:** [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC]  
**Reviewed by:** [Human reviewer name, if applicable]  
**Status:** [Draft / Reviewed / Approved / Archived]

⚠️ **GUARDRAIL: This is an AI-generated report. See "Limitations & Confidence" section below.**
```

---

## Content Structure

### 1. Executive Summary

- **One-sentence conclusion:** State the main finding or recommendation clearly.
- **Confidence level:** ✓ High / ≈ Medium / ⚠ Low / ❓ Uncertain
- **Evidence basis:** Cite the data/sources used (e.g., "Based on 50 benchmark runs on 3 devices").

**Example:**
> Gemma 3 1B Q4_K_M is the recommended model for 4GB-tier devices.
> 
> **Confidence:** ✓ High (based on measured inference speed <3s TTFT, battery <10%/hr on 2 Tier A devices)  
> **Evidence:** Benchmark results from bench/results/, quality evaluation scores, battery logs

---

### 2. Methodology

**Required sections:**

- **Data sources:** Where did the data come from? (e.g., benchmark harness, manual testing, third-party reports)
- **Sample size:** How many runs, devices, prompts? (e.g., "N=50 inference runs across 3 devices")
- **Measurement tools:** What was used to measure? (e.g., "llm_llamacpp profiler, Android Battery Historian")
- **Assumptions:** What did we assume to be true? (e.g., "Assumed device idle state before each run")
- **Limitations:** What could affect the results? (e.g., "Battery measurement is approximate ±2%; thermal throttling not controlled")

**Example:**
```markdown
## Methodology

**Data sources:**
- Benchmark harness: `bench/bin/bench.dart` (GGUF model loading + inference)
- Device logs: Android logcat, battery stats
- Manual evaluation: 3 human raters scoring output quality on 20 prompts

**Sample size:**
- 50 inference runs per model per device
- 3 Tier A devices (4GB RAM, Android 11–12)
- 20 academic prompts (math, physics, biology, etc.)

**Measurement tools:**
- Load time: `llm_llamacpp` native profiler (milliseconds)
- Decode speed: token count / elapsed time (tokens/sec)
- Battery: Android Battery Historian + manual drain measurement
- Quality: Blind 1–5 scoring (summarization, reasoning, factual accuracy)

**Assumptions:**
- Device in idle state before each run
- No background apps consuming CPU/GPU
- Network disabled (airplane mode)
- Room temperature ~25°C

**Limitations:**
- Battery measurement is manual and approximate (±2%)
- Thermal throttling not actively controlled; results may vary in hot environments
- Quality evaluation is subjective; inter-rater reliability not measured
- iOS results deferred (no macOS available)
```

---

### 3. Results / Findings

**Format:** Use tables, charts, or structured data. Always include units and confidence intervals where applicable.

**Example:**
```markdown
## Results

| Model | Device | Load (ms) | TTFT (ms) | Decode (tok/s) | Peak RSS (MB) | Confidence |
|-------|--------|-----------|-----------|----------------|---------------|-----------|
| Gemma 3 1B | Pixel 6a | 1200 | 450 | 26 | 850 | ✓ High |
| Llama 3.2 1B | Pixel 6a | 1500 | 520 | 20 | 920 | ✓ High |
| SmolLM3 1.7B | Pixel 6a | 1800 | 580 | 18 | 1100 | ✓ High |

**Notes:**
- TTFT = Time to first token (lower is better)
- Decode = sustained generation speed
- Peak RSS = maximum resident set size during inference
- Confidence = based on sample size (N=50 runs per model)
```

---

### 4. Analysis & Interpretation

**Required:**
- What do the results mean?
- Are there patterns or outliers?
- What could explain the differences?
- What are alternative interpretations?

**Example:**
```markdown
## Analysis

**Key findings:**

1. **Gemma 3 1B is fastest:** 26 tok/s decode speed, lowest TTFT (450ms).
   - Likely due to optimized quantization (Q4_K_M) and efficient architecture.
   - Meets the <3s response target (TTFT + ~30 tokens = 450 + 1150 = 1600ms).

2. **SmolLM3 1.7B has higher RAM footprint:** 1100 MB peak vs 850 MB for Gemma 3 1B.
   - Larger model (1.7B params) requires more KV cache.
   - Still fits within 4GB budget (OS + app ~2.5GB, model ~1.1GB = 3.6GB total).

3. **Battery drain is acceptable:** All models <10%/hr on sustained inference.
   - Gemma 3 1B: ~7%/hr (best)
   - SmolLM3 1.7B: ~9%/hr (acceptable)

**Alternative interpretations:**
- Vulkan backend might improve SmolLM3 performance on newer devices (not tested).
- Thermal throttling could reduce decode speed in hot environments (not measured).
- Quality differences might favor SmolLM3 for reasoning tasks (subjective evaluation pending).
```

---

### 5. Limitations & Confidence

**Critical section — always include:**

```markdown
## Limitations & Confidence

### Verified ✓
- Load time, TTFT, decode speed (measured directly)
- Peak RSS (profiler data)
- Model runs without OOM on Tier A devices

### Estimated ≈
- Battery drain (manual measurement, ±2% uncertainty)
- Quality scores (subjective, 3 raters, no inter-rater reliability measured)
- Generalization to other devices (only tested on 3 devices)

### Assumed ⚠
- Device idle state before runs (not actively verified)
- No thermal throttling during testing (room temp ~25°C)
- Quantization quality loss is acceptable for tutoring (not validated with users)

### Not Tested ❌
- iOS performance (requires macOS/Xcode)
- Vulkan backend on mid-range devices
- Long-term battery drain (>1 hour sustained inference)
- Multi-turn conversation quality (only single-turn prompts tested)
- RAG integration (not yet implemented)

### Confidence Summary

| Claim | Confidence | Reason |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Gemma 3 1B meets <3s TTFT target | ✓ High | Direct measurement, N=50 runs |
| Battery drain <10%/hr | ≈ Medium | Manual measurement, limited sample |
| Quality acceptable for tutoring | ⚠ Low | Subjective evaluation, no user validation |
| Generalizes to all 4GB devices | ⚠ Low | Only tested on 3 devices |
```

---

### 6. Recommendations

**Format:** Classify by importance.

```markdown
## Recommendations

### Critical (Required before Phase 1)
- [ ] Validate quality with actual tutoring use case (e.g., 10 students, 1 week)
- [ ] Test on 2–3 additional Tier A devices to confirm generalization

### High (Strongly recommended)
- [ ] Implement Vulkan backend for mid-range Android devices
- [ ] Measure inter-rater reliability for quality evaluation
- [ ] Test long-term battery drain (2+ hour sustained inference)

### Medium (Nice to have)
- [ ] Benchmark iOS performance once macOS is available
- [ ] Compare with LiteRT-LM GPU backend on Snapdragon 8 Gen 2+
- [ ] Evaluate RAG integration impact on inference speed

### Low (Future enhancement)
- [ ] Fine-tune model for academic tutoring domain
- [ ] Implement speculative decoding for faster generation
```

---

## Guardrails Checklist

Use this checklist before finalizing any AI-generated report:

- [ ] **Confidence levels assigned** to all major claims (✓ High / ≈ Medium / ⚠ Low / ❓ Uncertain)
- [ ] **Evidence cited** for each claim (e.g., "Based on N=50 runs")
- [ ] **Limitations section** explicitly lists what was NOT tested
- [ ] **Assumptions documented** (e.g., "Device idle state assumed")
- [ ] **Alternative interpretations** considered (e.g., "Vulkan might improve performance")
- [ ] **Verified vs. Estimated vs. Assumed** clearly distinguished
- [ ] **No unsupported claims** (e.g., "Production-ready", "Scales to 1M users")
- [ ] **Recommendations classified** by importance (Critical / High / Medium / Low)
- [ ] **Human review required** before "Approved" status
- [ ] **Timestamp & generator noted** in header (AI model, date, reviewer)

## When NOT to Use AI Reports

- **Security-critical decisions** (e.g., auth, encryption) — require human expert review
- **User-facing claims** (e.g., "100% privacy", "Never crashes") — require legal/product review
- **Financial decisions** (e.g., cost projections, pricing) — require business owner approval
- **Medical/health claims** (e.g., "Improves learning outcomes") — require clinical validation

In these cases, use AI for **analysis only**, and require explicit human sign-off before publication.

---

## Questions?

If you're unsure about confidence levels or limitations, ask:
- "What evidence supports this claim?"
- "What could make this wrong?"
- "What did we NOT test?"
- "Is this verified, estimated, or assumed?"

**When in doubt, mark it as ⚠ Low confidence or ❌ Not tested.**
